k-1.x_notes: All mathematics checks out (traps 3,6,9,12; {1,2,3} traps 4,8,12; game record in P5 has a unique error at row 3; 9 counters -> let the adult go first; two-pile answers (2,2),(5,5),(4,1) second and (2,1),(3,1) first are correct). Strengths: counter pictures on numbered cards for piles 1-12 are very concrete for kindergartners; P5 (find the mistake in a played game) and P6 (choose who starts against the adult) are lively and concrete; P7 asks for traps beyond 20; P9 two-pile set includes the non-obvious (4,1). Weaknesses: opening is thin and dumbed down (P1 is trivial yes/yes/no, P2 is a single yes/no, P4 is a two-blank directed tree), which is the organizer's stated K-1 complaint; Name field on every page; header lacks the activity title and the footer is just a page number; two boxed rule/definition panels; lots of empty page space.
k-1.y_notes: All mathematics checks out (P1 moves 1,2,cross,1,2; P2 6 and 9 second, 7 and 8 first; P3 take 1, take 2, cross 12; traps 3,6,...,18; Ben's take-2 opening wins only from 5, 8, 11; game sequences number 5 and 8; {1,2,3} traps 4,8,...,20; two-pile answers correct; misere traps 1,4,7,...,19). Strengths: starts at a real level (P1 asks for the winning move or a cross for each pile, not just yes/no); tests a greedy plan (Ben); asks for the copying strategy with two piles of 6; adds the misere rule as a contrasting variant; consistent header/footer, no Name field, one shared rule line. Weaknesses: the 1-20 trap grids (P4, P7, P10) are bare numbers, less concrete for kindergartners than X's pictured cards, and three such grids feel repetitive; P6 (enumerate game sequences) is a slight tangent and gives 8 and 10 rows for 5 and 8 answers; denser serif text.
k-1.reason: Y gives K-1 more real thinking from the first problem and runs the full session (greedy plan, mirror strategy, misere variant), avoiding the thin opening X has; X's pictures and game-record problem are nice but do not offset its trivial start and format problems.

grades-2-3.x_notes: Correct throughout ({1,3,4} losing piles 2,7,9,14,16; 23,28,100 L and 33,50 W; {1,3,5} losing = evens; two-pile {1,3,4} answers (5,5),(7,2),(6,4) second and (6,1),(9,8) first). Strengths: goes straight to the outline's {1,3,4} rule with a play-first P1; the take-4 claim (fails at 5) and the copy claim at 8 test strategies directly; P5 game-record analysis (turns 2 and 3) and P6 full plan from 14 are excellent 'every reply' tasks; P7 extends to 100. Weaknesses: P5 wording ('could have taken a different number and then been sure to win') literally also fits turns 4 and 6; two-pile {1,3,4} cases like (6,4) and (9,8) are very hard for third graders without values; Name field, nonstandard header/footer, boxed definitions.
grades-2-3.y_notes: Correct throughout ({1,2} table; Lee right, Mo wrong; Jo's 7 is losing for partner with full answer tree, Kai's 8 is not; {1,3,4} 1-20 with moves; 30 and 100 second, 50 take 1, 61 take 3; {1,3,5} evens; two-pile {1,2} answers; P8 has {1,2,3,4} and alternates such as {1,2,3,4,6}). Strengths: gentle {1,2} on-ramp then {1,3,4}; claims to test (Lee/Mo, Jo/Kai) match the outline's emphasis; tables for recording both 'first or second' and the winning move; two-pile work with {1,2} is accessible and asks for the copying argument; P8 inverse problem (invent a rule whose losing piles are multiples of 5, then another) is an excellent open capstone; header/footer follow the standard, no Name field. Weaknesses: P3 is a long paragraph for 3rd graders; small boxes in P4/P6; P7 has only four cases.
grades-2-3.reason: Both are strong and correct; Y's sequence of claims to test, its more level-appropriate two-pile work, and the invent-a-rule capstone give it a slight edge over X's excellent but occasionally over-hard or ambiguous items.

grades-4-5.x_notes: Correct and ambitious: {1,3,4} period 7; greedy-first wins only from 1,3,4,6,11 (a nice finite answer); {1,3,5}-equivalent sets are all sets of odd numbers; {1,2,m} keeps multiples of 3 iff 3 does not divide m, otherwise period m+1; {1,6,9} repeats from 10 with cycle 5; pigeonhole periodicity; mex values 0,1,0,1,2,3,2; two-pile answers (6,4),(12,5) lose, (5,1) take 4 from 5, (11,3) take 1 from 11; equal-values proof. Strengths: deep arc reaching Sprague-Grundy values and eventual periodicity with a preperiod. Weaknesses: entirely abstract and proof-heavy from P1 on (no play, no concrete entry), several items (P5 general m, P7 pigeonhole for every finite set, P10) are a stretch for two 4th graders and a 5th grader; ten problems is more than 40 minutes; mid-packet definition box; Name field and nonstandard header/footer.
grades-4-5.y_notes: Correct: {1,3,4} 1-24 with moves; 100 losing, 1000 take 4, 2026 take 1 or 3; {1,2} and {1,2,4} both multiples of 3, {1,4} 0/2 mod 5, {1,3,5} evens; greedy fails in {1,2} (4), {1,3,4} (5), {1,4} (8) and works in {1,3,5}; multiples-of-4 games are {1,2,3},{1,2,3,5},{1,2,3,6},{1,2,3,5,6}; misere losing piles shift by one (1 mod 3; 1,3 mod 7); two-pile grids with {1,2} and {1,3,4} (unequal P-pairs (1,3),(1,8),(3,8),(2,7),(4,6)). Strengths: concrete entry (table of first/second and moves), purposeful rule comparisons including {1,2,4} vs {1,2}, greedy tested across four games, complete classification problem, misere contrast, 2D grid discovery that unequal piles can be losing; standard header/footer. Weaknesses: stops short of values and general periodicity; small numerals in strip grids; no explicit play prompt until P9.
grades-4-5.reason: X reaches deeper ideas but is abstract and proof-heavy from the start for this group; Y covers the outline's 4-5 emphasis with a concrete entry and well-chosen contrasting rules, making it slightly more likely to keep all three children productively engaged.

overall.reason: Y is preferable in every band: its K-1 pages start at a real level and fill the session, its 2-3 pages test strategies and end with a strong open problem, and its 4-5 pages offer a concrete entry with good rule comparisons. Both packets are mathematically correct, but X has a thin K-1 opening, an abstract proof-heavy 4-5 packet, and Name fields and nonstandard headers throughout, so it would need more editing in fifteen minutes.
